name: IR2101STRPBF
title: 600 V high- and low-side gate driver
summary: IR2101 and IR2102 are monolithic drivers for a pair of N-channel MOSFETs or IGBTs: one output referred to ground and one on a floating channel that rides on an offset of up to 600 V, supplied by a bootstrap capacitor. The outputs source 130 mA and sink 270 mA minimum and the two channels' delays match within 50 ns. Inputs accept 3.3 V, 5 V and 15 V logic; the IR2101 outputs follow their inputs and the IR2102 outputs invert them. Each comes in 8-lead PDIP or 8-lead SOIC (S suffix), with lead-free versions (PbF).

circuits.title: Typical connection, IR2101
circuits.description: The IR2101 drives one half-bridge leg of two N-channel MOSFETs from a single VCC rail. VCC is decoupled to COM and charges the bootstrap capacitor between VB and VS through a diode while the low-side switch holds VS near ground; that capacitor then powers the high-side output. HO and LO reach the gates through series resistors. The high-side drain sits on a rail of up to 600 V with its own capacitor to ground, the midpoint leaves to the load, and the two active-high logic inputs and COM share the ground of the low-side source.

circuits.title: Typical connection, IR2102
circuits.description: The IR2102 drives one half-bridge leg of two N-channel MOSFETs from a single VCC rail. VCC is decoupled to COM and charges the bootstrap capacitor between VB and VS through a diode while the low-side switch holds VS near ground; that capacitor then powers the high-side output. HO and LO reach the gates through series resistors. The high-side drain sits on a rail of up to 600 V with its own capacitor to ground, the midpoint leaves to the load, and the two active-low logic inputs and COM share the ground of the low-side source.

operation.text: Two independent output channels: LO is referred to COM and powered from VCC; HO is referred to VS and powered from the floating VB-VS supply, so it can drive the gate of a high-side N-channel MOSFET or IGBT whose source sits at up to 600 V. The floating channel is meant to be supplied by a bootstrap diode and capacitor. It tolerates negative transients on VS and is dV/dt immune; the allowable VS slew is 50 V/ns.

IR2101: HO follows HIN and LO follows LIN, each output high while its input is high. IR2102: the inputs are active low, so HO is high while /HIN is low and LO is high while /LIN is low. The inputs take standard CMOS or LSTTL levels down to 3.3 V logic: a high is at least 3 V and a low at most 0.8 V across VCC = 10 V to 20 V. The two channels are independent. Each IR2101 input has a resistor to COM inside the part; each IR2102 input has a resistor to VCC.

Turn-on delay ton runs from the input's 50 % point to the output reaching 10 %; rise time tr is the output going from 10 % to 90 %. Turn-off delay toff runs from the input's 50 % point to the output falling to 90 %; fall time tf is from 90 % to 10 %. Delay matching MT is the difference between the high-side and low-side delays for the same edge.
VCC has an undervoltage lockout. Its rising threshold VCCUV+ is 8 V to 9.8 V (8.9 V typ) and its falling threshold VCCUV- is 7.4 V to 9 V (8.2 V typ).
The high-side command crosses to the floating channel as pulses through a high-voltage level shifter; a pulse filter and an RS latch on the floating side rebuild the state that drives HO.

Each output is a pulse-current buffer built to keep shoot-through inside the driver low. With 15 V bias it sources at least 130 mA (210 mA typ) into a shorted output and sinks at least 270 mA (360 mA typ), for pulses up to 10 µs. Into 1000 pF the rise time is 100 ns typ and the fall time 50 ns typ.

Lead-free parts carry the part number, a date code (year and work week), a lot code with a four-digit code, and an assembly site code. A 'P' in the marking code position marks a released lead-free part.
